newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends firm, awaits INRO entry.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends firm, awaits INRO entry.

text.p: Technical support and news of fresh SMR20 sales helped Malaysian rubber prices to end firm on Friday, after being bashed through the week on bearish factors, traders said.
"It's no relief, but hopefully the price might hold next week," said a trader.

The International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) was, meanwhile, getting ready to enter the market to buy rubber if its five-day indicator price touched the must-buy level of 172 cents. The indicator finished below the may-buy level of 183 cents on July 10.
A government trade source reported the sale of 1,000 tonnes of August SMR20 to China at 232 cents a kg and a similar consignment to Germany at 230 cents a kg.

The Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted the RSS1 buyer for August at 228 cents a kg, up one cent from Thursday. The board priced the SMR 20 buyer for August half cent higher at 232.50 cents.
Trading houses quoted the SMR CV at 299 cents, SMR L at 280, SMR5 at 244, SMR10 at 235 and latex at 198.
Some traders said if the market turned bearish again next week, the official price of the RSS1 could fall by another 10 cents and the SMR20 by around five cents.
The INRO's five-day indicator was at 182.48 cents a kg on July 10, compared to the 183.56 cents on July 9. The daily indicator ended at 181.42 against the previous 181.66.
Malaysia-based shipping brokers quoted freight rates for rubber from Malaysia to Rotterdam at $700 per 20-ft container, and $1,400 per 40-ft container.
